dataset.timestamp_unit: seconds since the first message (2004-04-15 07:56:01 UTC)
dataset.node_id_mapping: identity: TGB node id n -> TGN memory slot n (slot 0 unused)
dataset.direction: sender -> receiver as stored in the file

split.method: chronological, by timestamp quantile (as in TGN/CoDy)

model.name: TGN (event-level)
model.raw_message: constant 1.0 per event (UCI has no edge features)

inference.protocol: sequential: every history event is replayed one at a time, in event-id order, from a reset memory
inference.score: sigmoid(logit) of the TGN link predictor for (A, B) at t
inference.decision_rule: predicted class = 'message' when logit > 0 (probability > 0.5); CoDy's own counterfactual criterion is a sign change of this logit

target_selection.rule: seeded permutation of test-split events; take the first event that is eligible
eligibility: no other event shares its timestamp (history = strictly earlier)
both endpoints sent or received a message before t
the model predicts it correctly as a message (logit > 0)

preprocessing: read tgbl-uci_edgelist.csv columns u, i, ts (label and idx unused: label is always 0, idx is the 1-based row number)
event id = 0-based row position; rows are already sorted by ts
no events are filtered: the file has no self-loops
direction kept as stored (u = sender, i = receiver)
node ids used as memory slots directly (no remapping)
dataset.relation_to_cody_source: identical to Opsahl OCnodeslinks.txt (CoDy README source) minus its 1,899 self-loop rows; timestamps = unix time - 1082015761

split.method: chronological, by timestamp quantile (as in TGN/CoDy)

model.implementation: compare_explainers.tgn_backend.EventTgn (core.TgnModel GraphAttentionEmbedding + LinkPredictor; PyG TGNMemory, IdentityMessage, LastAggregator, LastNeighborLoader)

configuration.name: TGN (event-level)
configuration.raw_message: constant 1.0 per event (UCI has no edge features)

training.negative_sampling: uniform random destination node id, seeded

evaluation.protocol: sequential replay; one seeded uniform-random negative destination per held-out event; balanced, so chance AP/AUC/accuracy = 0.5

model.why_not_the_existing_tgap_tgn_adapter: core.TgnModel.TgnTemporalGraphModel reads snapshots (time = snapshot index) and returns the MEAN probability of the last snapshot's edges; it scores no single link and keeps no checkpoint. CoDy explains one event of an event stream, so it cannot query that adapter without changing its semantics. One event-level TGN built from the same modules is trained instead and both explainers call it.

target.ground_truth: the message A -> B was observed at t (positive link, label 1)
target.selection_rule: seeded permutation of test-split events; take the first event that is eligible
eligibility: no other event shares its timestamp (history = strictly earlier)
both endpoints sent or received a message before t
the model predicts it correctly as a message (logit > 0)

baseline_protocol: three independent paths: target-selection stream pass, TGAP's baseline call, CoDy's original-score computation

plan.definition: mean Jaccard distance between each earlier snapshot's edge set and the latest snapshot's edge set (0 = history identical to the present, 1 = completely different); ChurnTransformation.propertyValue
plan.temporal_scope: snapshots 1-17 (all history before the latest 10-day window)
constraints: the latest snapshot is kept exactly (TGAP's Churn anchor)
every snapshot keeps its node set and edge count (remove-one-add-one swaps)
no community constraint (communities=None): every edge is churn-eligible
lift to events keeps the number, timing and order of events; only the addressee pair of swapped messages changes

feasibility.cause: Every requested swap was possible in every earlier period.
feasibility.measure_note: Churn is a ratio (Jaccard distance), so swapping a share of edges does not change it by exactly the same share.

feasibility.cause: In 6 of 17 earlier periods fewer swaps were possible than requested, because the latest period has only a limited number of connections that can be copied into the past.
feasibility.measure_note: Churn is a ratio (Jaccard distance), so swapping a share of edges does not change it by exactly the same share.

cody.sparsity_definition: explanation size / candidate size (CoDy repository, evaluate_factual_subgraphs.py)

comparability.label: scientific comparison: same model, same input, same original score
